text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were expected to retain their firm bias on Wednesday after spending much of Tuesday afternoon trading in narrow, but higher ranges. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.23, up 0.15 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts edged up slightly at the close after a static day which saw little movement after an initial morning mark-up, as investors remained cautious ahead of the UK budget on November 26. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-21/32, up 7/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures continued their steady march towards fresh highs, buoyed by a positive German bond market, while December PIBOR finally breached the top of the trading range it has been stuck in for the past 19 sessions. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.04, up 0.18 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets presented a buoyant front at the close after a choppy day with volumes down compared with recent investor buying sprees. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.32, up 0.63 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices were steady at higher levels by midday as the market looks ahead to the next round of fresh supply. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-8/32, up 13/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.44 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese goverment bonds ended firmer, but surrendered most gains on dealers' profit-taking towards the close. Cash bond purchases by regional financial institutions as well as some city banks' portfolio accounts led the rally in the early afternoon.In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 125.32, up 0.20 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Turkey's 750 million mark five-year offering stood out among a plethora of new issues. German retail investors led the charge to snap up paper at the 280 b.p. reoffer level. The overnight move by Japan Credit Rating Agency to cut Turkey's yen debt one notch had little impact in Europe. TMCC set a $250 million three-year bond while NordLB tapped both the dollar and French franc sectors. NatWest launched a self-led 300 million sterling 15-year structured bond while BayerLB asked for 200 million sterling over five years.
